reader_prompt.target: A = RUMOR vs B = NON_RUMOR (source post plus the observed social evidence visible up to the cutoff)
reader_prompt.scoring: teacher-forced candidate log probability p_r(y|C), y in {A=RUMOR, B=NON_RUMOR}

utility_definition.formula: u_r(e) = p_r(gold | SRC) - p_r(gold | SRC without e)
utility_definition.gold: the dataset's frozen rumour/non-rumour label of the event the evidence belongs to

utility_meaning.positive: the evidence unit makes this reader more likely to answer with the dataset's gold rumour/non-rumour label for that event
utility_meaning.negative: the evidence unit makes this reader less likely to answer with that gold label
utility_meaning.claim_forbidden: fact-checking / truth-verification utility, or any claim that the evidence was shown to be true or false

maweibo.label_semantics: the event's rumour / non-rumour annotation carried by the frozen Ma-Weibo source (Ma et al., IJCAI 2016)
maweibo.boundary: the label is a rumour annotation, not a verified true/false verdict on the underlying claim

pheme.label_semantics: the event's rumour / non-rumour annotation carried by the frozen PHEME source (Zubiaga et al., PLOS ONE 2016)
pheme.boundary: rumour != false and non-rumour != true: PHEME annotates whether a claim circulated as an unverified rumour, not whether it is factually true or false

cross_dataset_boundary.note: Ma-Weibo and PHEME differ in platform, language, annotation process and claim distribution; M1-E measured a systematic E3 distribution shift, so the M1-F contrast must not be reported as a language-only shift

conclusion.reason: utility is defined over the reader's rumour/non-rumour answer agreement, so an evidence-level claim is supported provided it is stated as rumour-label utility and never as truth verification
